meta.purpose: A decision queue, not a to-do list. Each proposal says what it would change, what it costs, what it risks, and which earlier question has to be answered first. A reviewer can approve a row without reading the whole site.
meta.how_to_use: Read the 'depends on' column before the 'effort' column. Anything depending on Q-03 or Q-10 cannot be approved first, because approving it would spend effort on traffic that earns nothing.
meta.recommended_first: S-01 and S-07 still come first: one confirms the site can earn, the other makes it findable. S-24 to S-27 are the follow-on set added on 2026-11-20; S-22, S-23 and S-24 are already implemented and are kept here so a reviewer can reject them in writing.
meta.implemented_note: Rows marked implemented were completed on 2026-11-20 and are kept visible with the evidence, so the record of what changed is not just a changelog nobody reads.

paths.name: Shop first
paths.summary: Make the five product pages as good as they can be, then buy traffic or push it socially.
paths.before_you_choose: Product pages cannot show a price, so the page has to win on explanation alone. This path is honest but slow until a named author exists.
paths.good_if: You can name an editor and want the catalogue to carry the site.

paths.name: Publication first
paths.summary: Keep publishing question-shaped guides and let search traffic arrive before optimising anything.
paths.before_you_choose: Without Search Console this is writing into the dark. S-07 is 15 minutes and makes the rest measurable.
paths.good_if: You enjoy writing and can hold a cadence for three months.

paths.name: Measure first
paths.summary: Switch on analytics and Search Console, collect four weeks of data, then decide what to build.
paths.before_you_choose: Needs a host for the collector and a privacy statement. That is the only real cost.
paths.good_if: You would rather have one well-chosen page than eight guessed ones.

suggestions.title: Click one link, then read the Associates report
suggestions.why: The links do not carry the tag yet. What is still unknown is whether a Special Link from this account would be credited. That is a two-minute test with an answer either way.
suggestions.risk: None. It is a read-only check.

suggestions.title: Name an editor, or stop implying editorial authority
suggestions.why: A publication with no byline reads as generated, however careful it is. One named person with an accurate, modest bio is the cheapest credibility available and the thing a reader looks for first.
suggestions.risk: None, provided the bio describes work that actually happened. Claiming hands-on testing that did not occur would convert this site from careful to deceptive.

suggestions.title: Switch on Search Console and submit the sitemap
suggestions.why: The next topic should be chosen from queries that exist. Right now every subject is an editorial hypothesis, and the site cannot tell which of the eight guides anyone wanted.
suggestions.risk: None. Requires the owner's Google account, so it cannot be done by an agent.

suggestions.title: Apply for the Creators API — knowing it is gated behind 10 qualifying sales
suggestions.why: Program Policies §2(b) permits price and availability only where Amazon serves the data or it arrives through the Creators API or PA API. Amazon's own documentation now records PA-API 5 as deprecated and returning 403 AccessDeniedException, and lists the Creators API prerequisites as Associates enrolment plus at least 10 qualifying sales within the past 30 days. The policy text still names both APIs, so following the policy alone would aim at a route that no longer answers.
suggestions.effort: an application, plus qualifying sales on most accounts
suggestions.risk: Low, but the sequence is not negotiable: live prices arrive after the site proves it can sell, not before. A separate clause also requires a comparison-format price display to show the lowest used price as well as the lowest new, which is a second reason the comparison table stays blank.
suggestions.recommendation: Revisit the moment the sales count allows it; do not treat it as a build task

suggestions.title: Buy one air fryer, use it, and publish one genuinely tested comparison
suggestions.why: This is the single biggest jump in both usefulness and ranking potential. Every page in this category is assembled from seller copy; a page with a real measurement table and real photographs would be materially different.
suggestions.risk: Cost. Also, FTC guidance and the Associates policies require a review to be genuine, so the testing must actually happen before the page exists.
suggestions.recommendation: The highest-value single investment on this list

suggestions.title: Deploy the analytics endpoint, or delete it
suggestions.why: A measurement plan that never measures is decoration. Either host the collector with a retention statement and a privacy page, or remove the code so the claim stops implying something is coming.
suggestions.risk: Low, provided retention and IP handling are stated before the client is pointed at it.

suggestions.title: Do not commission more guides until S-03 or S-05 lands
suggestions.why: Eight guides already cover the decision space honestly. A ninth written from another hypothesis adds volume, not value, and raises the chance the whole publication is treated as one undifferentiated block.
suggestions.effort: none — it is a decision not to act
suggestions.risk: None. It is reversible the moment data arrives.
suggestions.recommendation: The least popular and most important item here

suggestions.title: Replace illustrations with photographs of the actual products
suggestions.why: Every image here is an illustration and labelled as one. A shop without product photography asks the reader to imagine the thing, which is exactly the gap a competitor fills.
suggestions.effort: an afternoon with a phone and a window, once a product is in hand
suggestions.risk: Tied to S-05: photographing a product you have not used is a step toward the thing this site avoids.

suggestions.title: Choose one of the three paths before doing any of the above
suggestions.why: The suggestions are individually sensible and collectively contradictory. 'Shop first' needs photography; 'publication first' needs cadence; 'measure first' needs analytics. Picking a path is what turns this page into a plan.
suggestions.risk: Doing nothing is also a choice, and it is the one that leaves the site as it is.
suggestions.recommendation: Pick a path, then only read that path's rows

suggestions.title: Publish a dated change log on the site
suggestions.why: A publication that visibly changes is a publication someone returns to. It also makes 'reviewed on' meaningful rather than decorative.
suggestions.risk: None.

suggestions.title: Buy a domain and move off the repository subpath
suggestions.why: Every link on this site is relative because it lives at /Affil1/. A domain removes that constraint, gives the brand somewhere to live, and makes the canonical URL something a reader could say out loud.
suggestions.effort: a purchase, DNS, a CNAME file, one constant in the build
suggestions.risk: Low, if redirects are handled. Doing it after links circulate is more annoying than doing it now.

suggestions.title: Set a fortnightly publishing cadence and put it in the workflow document
suggestions.why: Organic traffic rewards consistency more than brilliance. One guide a fortnight is achievable at the current standard and is enough to keep the feed and the sitemap alive.
suggestions.risk: A cadence with no author behind it becomes a fiction. Do S-02 first.

suggestions.title: Rewrite the storefront in a shop voice instead of an audit voice
suggestions.why: The previous front page led with verification process and repeated 'not tested' on every card. A reader arrives wanting to know what to buy, and left knowing what could not be proven.
suggestions.risk: Reduced: the provenance detail was moved one click away, not deleted.
suggestions.evidence: index.html; the audit material now lives on review/ and about/

suggestions.title: Replace plain listing links with account-validated Special Links, one product at a time, and keep the build refusing anything else
suggestions.why: Program Policies 2(b) requires the Associates ID as a parameter. The earlier build emitted bare /dp/ URLs with no tag, which cannot be attributed to any account.
suggestions.risk: None; it is enforced in one function and checked on every build.
suggestions.evidence: _tools/layout.py buy_url(); tag rule in _tools/check.py; see FLG-009

suggestions.title: Consolidate two competing editions into one canonical site
suggestions.why: The repository served a generated edition at the root and a hand-written one under crisp/, plus duplicate root pages covering the same products. Two sites describing five products cannot both be the answer.
suggestions.risk: The other edition was archived rather than deleted, and every archived page carries a noindex tag.

suggestions.title: Publish P-04 as a thermometer instead of an unresolved row
suggestions.why: The fourth link resolves to a ThermoMaven digital meat thermometer. Leaving it as 'unresolved' kept a live product off the site and kept a false gap in the catalogue.
suggestions.risk: None. The earlier failure is documented rather than erased.

suggestions.title: Add structured data, breadcrumbs and share images
suggestions.why: Search engines and social previews both need machine-readable structure. The site had none beyond a WebSite block on the front page.
suggestions.risk: Reduced: the Article schema names the organization, not an invented person.
suggestions.evidence: BreadcrumbList and Article blocks on every guide and product page; og:image on every page

suggestions.title: Give the front page a seasonal feature and a reader channel
suggestions.why: A publication has a current issue. The hosting guide is featured on the front page, and RSS is offered as the way to come back — since no mailing list exists.
suggestions.risk: None. The RSS block says plainly that there is no mailing list.

suggestions.title: Request sub-tag Associate IDs so attribution comes from Amazon's own report
suggestions.why: Program Policies §2(b) allows Amazon to issue additional sub-tag Associate IDs on request so an Associate can “monitor and optimize the performance” of different links. A sub-tag per page turns “which guide earns?” into a question Amazon's own report answers, which is far stronger evidence than anything a first-party counter can produce. The same clause forbids tying a sub-tag to an identified visitor, which this site does not do.
suggestions.effort: a support request, then a small change to how each page builds its outbound links
suggestions.risk: Low. Sub-tags are subject to Amazon's approval, so the answer may be no, and nothing else on the site depends on it. It complements S-01 rather than replacing it: S-01 proves a click is credited at all, sub-tags say which page earned it.
suggestions.recommendation: Request it in the same dashboard session as S-01

suggestions.title: Schedule the link re-check so drift is reported rather than discovered
suggestions.why: Every product fact on this site rests on a supplied link resolving to the same listing it did on 2026-11-20. P-04 already showed that the same link can return a product page on one attempt and Amazon's continuity page on another, on the same date. The repository already has the tool for this (_tools/verify_links.py); what is missing is a schedule and a place for the result.
suggestions.effort: an hour to wire the existing tool into a scheduled run and publish its output
suggestions.risk: Medium, and worth stating plainly: an unattended re-check can hit the same interstitial P-04 did, and a false alarm is worse than no alarm. Any automated check must report the outcome and let a human adjudicate. It must never overwrite a verified record on its own.
suggestions.recommendation: Build it to report, never to rewrite

suggestions.title: Do not buy paid search, and do not use Amazon marks in any promotion
suggestions.why: Program Policies prohibit purchasing, registering or using any Amazon Mark in a search engine, disqualify purchases arriving through a paid search placement, and state that Associates must not use their tags to claim commissions from another programme on the same traffic. The site also has no measurement that could attribute a click, so paid acquisition would spend money that cannot be accounted for.
suggestions.effort: zero — this is a decision not to spend
suggestions.risk: None from complying. The risk is entirely in ignoring it, and it falls on the account rather than on a page.
suggestions.recommendation: Adopt as policy and leave it on this page as a recorded refusal

suggestions.title: Publish three guides whose only facts are a government page and the seller's own title
suggestions.why: The journal had ten decision guides and no article answering the questions a buyer types at the moment of doubt: is this chicken done, is my thermometer lying, what do I do with the food that sat out. Each of the three new guides is anchored to an official page read on 2026-11-20, so the site can be useful without inventing a test result it does not have.
suggestions.effort: one session: three articles, three commissioned illustrations, sitemap, feed and internal links regenerated by the existing build
suggestions.risk: Health-adjacent copy next to buy buttons. Contained by quoting rather than advising, linking every figure, and stating on each page that nothing was tested. Q-26 asks the owner to accept or narrow the rule.
suggestions.recommendation: Keep. Extend the same sourcing rule to every future guide.

suggestions.title: Make the second edition a non-indexed annex instead of deleting it
suggestions.why: Two branded publications of the same five listings were both indexable on one host, which is the one thing a small site cannot afford. The annex also holds registers another session wrote, so deleting it would have destroyed reviewable evidence to solve a routing problem.
suggestions.effort: one template change in the annex generator, plus three assertions added to its verifier
suggestions.risk: noindex means the annex pages will leave the results within days. They stay reachable by URL and from the shop's review pages, so nothing is lost to a reviewer.
suggestions.recommendation: Keep, then decide fold-or-retire on Q-16 rather than leaving two brands indefinitely.

suggestions.title: Make every CI gate fail when it tests nothing
suggestions.why: The pipeline's own evidence was inflated: a step that discovered CPython's stdlib tests reported 45 passes while running none of this repository's platform tests, and another checked a collector's syntax while the module could not import. Both are fixed, and each step now fails if discovery is empty - a state that previously read as success.
suggestions.risk: A previously silent step can now fail a build. That is the point; it has been run green locally first.
suggestions.recommendation: Keep. Apply the same rule to any future step that counts tests rather than asserting names.

suggestions.title: Publish one question-shaped guide a week under the same sourcing rule
suggestions.why: Thirteen guides is enough to be read as a publication and too few to be read as an authority. The topic bank on suggestions/design.html already ranks candidate questions; a cadence turns it into a habit, and the measured queries (once Q-11 and Q-15 land) decide the order rather than instinct.
suggestions.effort: one article a week: a guide that either quotes an official page or restricts itself to the seller's listing wording
suggestions.risk: Cadence without a source rule is how this repository got its first flagged register. If a week has no citable answer, the week is skipped and the gap is recorded.
suggestions.recommendation: Adopt, starting with the two remaining topic-bank questions that need no new sourcing: reheating without a microwave, and what a dehydrate setting claims.

suggestions.title: Collapse the three collectors to one before any measurement is promised
suggestions.why: The brief asks for click and conversion measurement first, and the repository currently holds three collectors with three different page vocabularies, one of which reads a register path that no longer exists and therefore fails closed forever. Publishing a dashboard on top of that would produce numbers no one can trace.
suggestions.effort: one decision, two files archived, the surviving one wired to the client and to the ledger importer
suggestions.risk: Choosing wrong costs a refactor; choosing nothing costs the ability to answer which page earns.
suggestions.recommendation: Decide Q-25 first, then delete or archive the rest with a note explaining which session wrote them.

suggestions.title: Run the ice-water check on the two linked thermometers and publish the result
suggestions.why: Every page on this site can only quote. One thermometer, one glass of ice water and a thermometer you already own would produce the first observation this publication could call its own, and the FSIS procedure for it is documented, cheap and reversible - it asks nothing of an account, a host or an API.
suggestions.effort: one afternoon and the cost of a fold-out dial thermometer for comparison; no equipment the kitchen does not have
suggestions.risk: The result describes one unit of one listing, so it must be published as a dated observation about an object, not a verdict about a product line. Amazon's policies bar misleading claims about a Product; a single unit's reading is not evidence about the model.
suggestions.depends_on: Q-24 (the same budget question, one tier down)
suggestions.recommendation: Cheaper and faster than S-05's full appliance purchase; worth doing as the pilot for any self-test policy.
